transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-30 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Head of ML - Trident), Marco Diaz (Platform Eng), Jenna Park (PM)

Summary (auto): initial model selection & infra fit, discuss context length and tool-calling, surface security requirements.

[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, um start to finish maybe 45, 50 minutes, we'll run through a few questions about your workloads and then Samir will go through some perf notes.
[00:00:12] Priya: thanks Alex. quick context — we're building an insight assistant for enterprise clients, a mix of document Q&A, long-form summarization, and a tool-calling layer that triggers retrieval and external API calls. Need strong multilingual support (EN/ES/FR at least) and some customers require 50k char contexts, so context length is a big one.
[00:00:35] Alex: great. and what's your target latency and throughput like, e.g. interactive sub-second vs batch?
[00:00:45] Marco: interactive for the UI — we want median latency under 800ms for short Q&A, but for long documents we can accept 2-4s per response. Throughput is moderate — maybe a few hundred requests per minute at peak.
[00:01:05] Jenna: timeline — PoC in the next 6 weeks, production decisions in Q4.

[00:01:20] Samir (SE): okay thanks, I'll ask a few clarifying things. You mentioned tool-calling — is that limited to vector DB retrieval or do you have external actions?
[00:01:30] Priya: both. retrieval first, plus triggers to our billing API and a few enrichment services, so we need deterministic tool calling and schema enforcement.
[00:01:46] Samir: cool. that maps well to Redwood's function-calling and structured output support. for model selection, do you have a preference for open models vs managed proprietary? we typically compare a few open checkpoints plus our Redwood-hosted curated variants.
[00:02:05] Priya: we prefer open models for auditability and cost, but we need performance parity — latency and hallucination controls. also encryption at rest and KMS keys for customer data is a must.

[00:02:20] Alex: understood. high level there are three modes — Hosted API (fast pilot), Dedicated (reserved capacity for predictable throughput) and Private (VPC / on-prem for strict compliance). Which mode are you leaning to?
[00:02:33] Marco: pilot on Hosted to move quick, but production will likely be Dedicated or Private depending on the security review. some enterprise clients insist on VPC peering.

[00:02:47] Samir: perfect. on models we usually benchmark across: 1) a 32k-context open LLM (we often test LlamaX-32k-style variants), 2) a 64k context variant for very long docs, and 3) a smaller fast embedding-optimized model for retrieval. For multilingual, we test mBERT-like embeddings vs multilingual open LLMs and also measure instruction-following in Spanish/French.
[00:03:13] Priya: can you share typical token costs and perf differences? our finance team cares about per-request economics.
[00:03:22] Samir: yes — we'll share a spreadsheet but high level: hosted with Redwood tends to be the fastest to set up and cheapest for low volume pilots. Dedicated gives better unit economics at scale because of reserved GPU pools and batching, but upfront commit. Private has the highest ops overhead but meets strict compliance and on-prem data residency. For 32k vs 64k context, compute jumps nonlinearly — roughly 1.8x to 2.5x cost depending on kernels and kv cache behavior.

[00:03:55] [00:04:00] Priya: hmm ok — what about tool-calling determinism? we need strong guarantees that calls won't get dropped and the output follows schema for downstream services.
[00:04:10] Alex: Redwood supports structured function/tool calling; we also offer replayable transcripts and per-request tracing in the Console so you can audit calls. For Dedicated/Private we can provide longer log retention and audit hooks.

[00:04:28] Marco: any gotchas with multilingual? some of our legacy models degrade in FR/ES for instruction-following.
[00:04:36] Samir: yep, language drift is real. We recommend fine-tuning or instruction-tuning steps, and in our benchmarks we test zero-shot and few-shot prompts in target languages. For embeddings we sometimes use language-specific encoders for better similarity. We can provide baseline evals for EN/ES/FR if you share a sample set.

[00:05:00] Jenna: are the open models you test quantized? we need to know memory footprint for Dedicated nodes.
[00:05:08] Samir: often yes — we run FP16 and int8 quantized variants in our tests. Memory and latency tradeoffs depend on kernel selection and whether KV caching is used. For Dedicated we show recommended instance sizes per model and sequence length.

[00:05:30] Priya: security — SOC 2 is a must, and we need SAML SSO for our team and customer-level RBAC if possible. Also encryption with customer-managed keys.
[00:05:43] Alex: Redwood is SOC 2 Type II and supports SAML SSO and RBAC; for Private we support customer KMS/HSM integrations. We'll include the security pack.

[00:05:55] Marco: curious about fallback policies — if capacity is constrained can Redwood auto-fallback to a cheaper or smaller model without breaking tool-calls?
[00:06:05] Samir: yes, routing policies can fallback to compatible model variants. However, for deterministic tool-calling you should pin the function signatures and have validation in the client. We'll walk through best practices in the tech deep dive.

[00:06:20] [00:06:30] Priya: about context length — some of our use cases need 50k characters, others up to 100k chars for large docs. do you support streaming long-context inputs or chunking strategies?
[00:06:43] Samir: we support both. For really long docs we recommend a retrieval-augmented approach: chunk indexing plus a vector DB. For cases needing full-context generation, we test 64k+ variants and recommend KV caching to speed repeated prefixes. That said, cost goes up. We'll include a sample cost calc.

[00:07:05] Jenna: can you show us a quick example of model outputs for Spanish summarization?
[00:07:12] Samir: I can paste a couple of short outputs after the call; for the demo we'll run a small live sample in the sandbox.

[00:07:20] Alex: to make this practical, could you share what success looks like — what acceptance criteria will you use for the PoC?
[00:07:28] Priya: accuracy on question answering (F1 on our eval set) > 85%, latency for short queries under 800ms p95, tool-calling reliability > 99% for a set of schema-bound calls, and cost under a target per-seat budget.

[00:07:50] Samir: noted, we can design benchmarks around those. One thing to call out: hallucination instrumentation — we have a quality monitoring feature that can surface regressions tied to prompt sets. We'll include that in the eval plan.

[00:08:05] Marco: for Dedicated, how do autoscaling and burst capacity look? during month-end reporting we can spike 3-4x.
[00:08:14] Alex: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst pools; we can size for steady-state and reserve extra for bursts. We'll propose a config.

[00:08:26] Priya: procurement and legal — do you have sample terms for data residency and indemnities?
[00:08:34] Alex: yes we'll send the standard enterprise addendum and a data processing agreement. For Private we can include stricter clauses.

[00:08:46] Jenna: what's the simplest path to get our infra folks comfortable? sometimes the ops team wants a network diagram and SAML flow.
[00:08:54] Marco: yep, and run a short smoke test for SSO.

[00:09:00] Samir: we'll include an infra diagram and SSO runbook. Also we can run a benchmark that simulates your sequence length distribution if you share a sampling of logs.

[00:09:18] Alex: ok let's recap next steps. We'll send pricing and SKUs, security pack, benchmark spreadsheet, and set up a technical deep-dive for Sep 6. We'll enable a hosted sandbox for you to run early tests.

[00:09:33] Priya: sounds good. I want Samir on the tech deep-dive, and Marco will bring infra details. Jenna will run product-side acceptance.

[00:09:45] Alex: perfect. any final quick q's?
[00:09:50] Priya: what's the expected lead time for Dedicated capacity if we commit?
[00:09:55] Alex: typically 2-4 weeks to provision reserved pools depending on region and instance types. For Private on-prem it's longer and depends on onboarding schedule.

[00:10:06] Marco: ok great. that's all from me.
[00:10:09] Jenna: thanks everyone.

[00:10:12] Alex: thanks, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

[00:10:18] [end of recorded transcript — auto-generated sections omitted].
